claim: Epic Games opened a rebuilt launcher preview with native Linux support and published provisional performance comparisons on October 14.
verifiedFacts: Epic's public launcher preview page offers Windows, macOS and native Linux installers.
Epic claims faster startup and navigation, but comparisons are vendor-measured.
Epic warns that feature parity is incomplete and trying the preview uninstalls the legacy launcher; competitive games are recommended on the legacy launcher.
inference: Mechanism: a parallel product preview exposes performance and parity tradeoffs before broad rollout; AI-assisted development was reported by the press but not established by the official preview page.
Consultancy relevance: measurable redesign/replatforming case study; buyer problem: balancing UI modernization, cross-platform coverage, performance and regressions.
Disposition: Design Standards CORE for performance/UX proof, portfolio INCUBATE as benchmark reference; avoid duplicating a game launcher.
Thesis movement: reinforces measured UX and lifecycle proof.
significance: A visible software preview offers an unusually explicit example of performance claims, missing-feature disclosure and rollout gates.
assumptions: Vendor benchmarks generalize across devices and real-world libraries.
knownLimitations: Official preview does not independently substantiate AI-written-code attribution.
Incomplete parity, and preview replaces legacy installation.
No independent performance and accessibility test.
